correctness.rationale: In arXiv:2609.27078v2, sprouts are finite but modal height and width count strict cluster links, not the cardinality of a reflexive cluster (Def 3.4); canonical sprout homomorphisms need not be injective (Def 7.1). Choose Sigma={p_bullet}, a reflexive Sigma-region bud representative Psi and a stable canonical one-cluster tree A whose bud image contains a finite representative set, as constructed via canonical Finality and Lemma 6.5. For each m≥1, B_m is the m-world reflexive complete modal cluster mapped constantly to Psi; the Sigma label is atomic and complete with no modal or intuitionistic defect. Its root is graftable, rho(B_m)=rho(w), hgt=wdt=0<3 and the tall-petal clause is vacuous. Distinct cardinalities imply nonisomorphism. Thus G contains infinitely many 3-petals modulo ordinary isomorphism. Def 8.2 limits simultaneous family grafting to finite G, whereas Prop 12.3 immediately grafts all. The gap is in that proof line, not a disproof of the proposition itself. Independent check: a complete reflexive cluster has no strict modal edge for every positive m, so duplicating a point preserves all relevant bounds.

evidence: Definition 3.4 defines strict height and width, neither of which counts elements of a single reflexive modal cluster.

Theorem 14.2 applies Kruskal to cluster label SETS, collapsing repetitions for a simulation quasiorder; it gives no bound on ordinary isomorphism classes.
The independent decision procedure proves the finite model property via different machinery, not the finiteness of the particular flower construction.

A future reduced-petal quotient might repair the construction, but such a quotient does not falsify the local counterexample.

value.rationale: The finite-petal premise is needed to define the stable flower in Proposition 12.3; the flower is invoked in the later internal-defect resolution and finite-model construction. This is a motivated structural proof-gap witness distinguishing ordinary isomorphism from the simulation quasiorder, not a mere renaming or an unsupported claim against the finite model property. It specifies an exact necessary repair boundary—control modal-cluster multiplicities or replace the all-isomorphism construction by a finite adequate family.

final_claim: For Sigma={p_bullet}, a stable canonical Sigma-tree with a bud w exists for which the ordinary-isomorphism classes of n=3 petals over w are infinite, witnessed by complete reflexive m-point clusters mapped constantly to a reflexive canonical point. Consequently Proposition 12.3’s displayed simultaneous graft of all petals is not licensed by the finite-family definition; this is only a local proof gap, not a counterexample to the theorem or IK4 FMP.
